classification.difficultyReason: Account for both arrival groups and the three absentees before identifying the late remainder, then express that remainder as both a count and a fraction of the whole class.

content.prompt: One-quarter of a class arrived at 7 p.m. for the school concert, half of the class arrived at 7.15 p.m., three children told the teacher that they were not able to attend, and the rest are running late. If there are 60 children in the class:

children.label: a
children.prompt: how many children arrived at 7 p.m.?

children.label: b
children.prompt: what fraction of the class are running late? How many children is this?

answer.worked:
Half of the whole class arrived at 7.15 p.m. The fraction unable to attend is $\frac{3}{60}=\frac1{20}$.
$$\begin{align*}1-\frac14-\frac12-\frac1{20}&=\frac{20}{20}-\frac5{20}-\frac{10}{20}-\frac1{20}\\1-\frac14-\frac12-\frac1{20}&=\frac4{20}\\1-\frac14-\frac12-\frac1{20}&=\frac15\\\frac15\times60&=12\end{align*}$$
$\frac15$ of the class, or 12 children, are running late.

children.label: c
children.prompt: what fraction told the teacher they were not able to attend the concert?

answer.worked:
$$\frac{3}{60}=\frac1{20}$$
$\frac1{20}$ of the class were unable to attend.
